decision: Every PR must be checked for rule violations and functionality absent from the graph; either finding must block merge.
why: Without a blocking check, rule violations and unnamed functionality can reach the default branch.
steps: Prerequisite: configure the check as required on the default branch, with no admin bypass.
On pull_request opened or synchronize, check out the PR head with full history.
Collect git diff origin/<base>...HEAD and the full content of non-deleted changed files. Exclude graph.md from injected content; cap injected content at 50 KB and mark truncation.
Run claude -p from the repository root so CLAUDE.md loads. Request a verdict for every foundation, constitutive rule, and regulative rule, including rules that do not apply.
Separately identify introduced functionality, capabilities, or resource types that no vocabulary, constitutive, or regulative node names.
Require JSON with result, summary: {what, why}, foundations, constitutive, regulative, and uncovered. Each uncovered entry must describe the gap and cite its introducing file and line.
Set the result to FAIL if any rule fails or uncovered is nonempty. A FAIL must fail the workflow job.
Render failures with violations and evidence, collapse passed rules by layer, and list uncovered findings separately.
Post the PR comment with the what/why summary, findings, model, token count, and cost in EUR.
violations: graph.md included in the injected file content.
